## 1.1 Parse Resolutions & Token Mapping

```{r parse-resolutions}
safe_parse_json <- function(x) tryCatch(fromJSON(x), error = function(e) NA)

df_parsed <- df %>%
  filter(closed == TRUE) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    outcomes_list = list(tryCatch(fromJSON(outcomes),       error = function(e) NA_character_)),
    prices_list   = list(tryCatch(fromJSON(outcome_prices), error = function(e) NA_character_)),
    tokens_list   = list(tryCatch(fromJSON(token_ids),      error = function(e) NA_character_))
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

df_binary <- df_parsed %>%
  mutate(
    n_outcomes = lengths(outcomes_list),
    is_binary  = n_outcomes == 2,
    yes_idx    = map_int(outcomes_list, ~ {
      idx <- which(tolower(.x) == "yes")
      if (length(idx) == 1) idx else NA_integer_
    })
  ) %>%
  filter(is_binary, !is.na(yes_idx)) %>%
  mutate(
    yes_token_id   = map2_chr(tokens_list, yes_idx, ~ .x[.y]),
    yes_resolution = map2_dbl(prices_list, yes_idx, ~ as.numeric(.x[.y])),
    no_idx         = ifelse(yes_idx == 1, 2, 1),
    no_token_id    = map2_chr(tokens_list, no_idx, ~ .x[.y])
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(yes_resolution), yes_resolution %in% c(0, 1))

cat(nrow(df_binary), "binary Yes/No markets with clean resolution\n")
cat("Resolution rate (Yes = 1):", round(mean(df_binary$yes_resolution), 3), "\n")
```

## 1.2 Derive Categories from Tags

```{r derive-categories}
category_rules <- tibble::tribble(
  ~category,       ~pattern,
  "Sports",        "nba|nfl|mlb|nhl|soccer|football|tennis|boxing|mma|ufc|cricket|esports|dota|league of legends|sports|epl|la liga|bundesliga|serie a|ligue 1|f1|formula|nascar|golf|olympics|pga",
  "Crypto",        "crypto|bitcoin|btc|ethereum|eth|solana|sol|defi|blockchain|token|nft|altcoin|memecoin|binance|coinbase",
  "Politics",      "politic|election|trump|biden|democrat|republican|congress|senate|governor|president|vote|gop|dnc|rnc|parliament|minister|legislation|bill|law|executive order",
  "Economics",     "econom|fed |federal reserve|interest rate|inflation|gdp|employment|jobs|recession|tariff|trade|stock market|s&p|nasdaq|dow jones|treasury|debt|cpi",
  "Science/Tech",  "science|tech|ai |artificial intelligence|openai|google|apple|microsoft|space|spacex|nasa|climate|weather|earthquake|hurricane|temperature",
  "Entertainment", "movie|film|oscar|grammy|emmy|music|album|box office|streaming|netflix|youtube|tiktok|celebrity|award|tv show|series",
  "World Events",  "war|conflict|ukraine|russia|china|israel|gaza|nato|united nations|refugee|disaster|pandemic",
  "Other",         ".*"
)

assign_category <- function(tags) {
  if (is.na(tags) || tags == "") return("Other")
  combined <- tolower(tags)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(category_rules))) {
    if (str_detect(combined, category_rules$pattern[i])) return(category_rules$category[i])
  }
  "Other"
}

df_binary <- df_binary %>%
  mutate(
    category    = map_chr(event_tags, assign_category),
    is_election = category == "Politics" &
      str_detect(tolower(event_tags),
        "trump|biden|harris|presidential|house|senate|congress|election 2024|midterm|ballot")
  )

cat("\n── Category distribution ──\n")
df_binary %>% count(category, sort = TRUE) %>% print()
cat("\nPolitics: election-tagged =",
    sum(df_binary$is_election, na.rm = TRUE), "/",
    sum(df_binary$category == "Politics"), "\n")
```

# 2 · Calibration Analysis (Snapshot Prices)

The core question: **when the market prices a Yes token at probability $p$, does the event actually happen $p$% of the time?**

```{r build-token-lookup}
token_lookup <- df_binary %>%
  select(yes_token_id, yes_resolution, id, event_title, category,
         is_election, closed_time, volume_num) %>%
  rename(token_id = yes_token_id) %>%
  mutate(closed_dt = ymd_hms(closed_time, quiet = TRUE)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(closed_dt))

yes_tokens <- unique(token_lookup$token_id)
cat(length(yes_tokens), "unique Yes tokens to look up\n")
```

```{r compute-time-snapshots, cache=TRUE}
dfp_arrow <- open_dataset(PRICE_FILE)

snapshots       <- c(1, 6, 24, 72, 168, 720)
snapshot_labels <- c("1h", "6h", "1d", "3d", "1w", "1mo")

BATCH_SIZE    <- 500
token_batches <- split(yes_tokens, ceiling(seq_along(yes_tokens) / BATCH_SIZE))
cat(length(token_batches), "batches of up to", BATCH_SIZE, "tokens\n")

get_snapshot_price <- function(hbc, price, target_hours) {
  diffs <- abs(hbc - target_hours)
  valid <- diffs < (target_hours * 0.5 + 1)
  if (!any(valid)) return(NA_real_)
  price[valid][which.min(diffs[valid])]
}

snapshot_list  <- vector("list", length(token_batches))
mkt_stats_list <- vector("list", length(token_batches))

for (i in seq_along(token_batches)) {
  batch_tokens <- token_batches[[i]]

  batch_prices <- dfp_arrow %>%
    filter(token_id %in% batch_tokens) %>%
    select(token_id, timestamp, price) %>%
    collect()

  if (nrow(batch_prices) == 0) next

  batch_prices <- batch_prices %>%
    inner_join(
      token_lookup %>% select(token_id, yes_resolution, id, category,
                               is_election, volume_num, closed_dt),
      by = "token_id"
    ) %>%
    mutate(hours_before_close = as.numeric(
      difftime(closed_dt, timestamp, units = "hours")
    )) %>%
    filter(hours_before_close >= 0)

  if (nrow(batch_prices) == 0) next

  # ── Snapshot prices ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  batch_snap <- batch_prices %>%
    group_by(token_id, id, yes_resolution, category, is_election, volume_num) %>%
    summarise(
      across_snapshots = list(tibble(
        snapshot_hours = snapshots,
        snapshot_label = snapshot_labels,
        snap_price     = map_dbl(snapshots, ~ get_snapshot_price(hours_before_close, price, .x))
      )),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    unnest(across_snapshots) %>%
    filter(!is.na(snap_price))

  snapshot_list[[i]] <- batch_snap

  # ── Per-market summary stats ────────────────────────────────────────
  mkt_summary <- batch_prices %>%
    arrange(token_id, desc(hours_before_close)) %>%
    group_by(token_id, id, yes_resolution, category, is_election, volume_num, closed_dt) %>%
    summarise(
      initial_price      = first(price),
      final_price        = last(price),
      min_price          = min(price),
      max_price          = max(price),
      price_range        = max(price) - min(price),
      n_obs              = n(),
      market_duration_h  = max(hours_before_close),
      price_sd           = if_else(n() > 2, sd(price), NA_real_),
      .groups            = "drop"
    )

  mkt_stats_list[[i]] <- mkt_summary

  if (i %% 5 == 0 || i == length(token_batches)) {
    cat(sprintf("  Batch %d/%d done (%d snapshot rows so far)\n",
                i, length(token_batches),
                sum(map_int(snapshot_list, ~ if (is.null(.x)) 0L else nrow(.x)))))
  }

  rm(batch_prices, batch_snap, mkt_summary); gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

snapshot_data <- bind_rows(snapshot_list)
market_stats  <- bind_rows(mkt_stats_list)
rm(snapshot_list, mkt_stats_list, dfp_arrow); gc()

cat("\n", nrow(snapshot_data), "total market × snapshot observations\n")
cat(nrow(market_stats), "markets with full price history stats\n")
```

## 2.1 Overall Calibration Curve

```{r calibration-curve-overall, fig.height=7}
calibration <- snapshot_data %>%
  mutate(
    price_bin    = cut(snap_price, breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.05),
                       include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE),
    bin_midpoint = (price_bin - 1) * 0.05 + 0.025
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(price_bin)) %>%
  group_by(snapshot_label, bin_midpoint) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), actual_pct = mean(yes_resolution), avg_price = mean(snap_price), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(snapshot_label = factor(snapshot_label, levels = c("1mo","1w","3d","1d","6h","1h")))

ggplot(calibration %>% filter(n >= 20), aes(x = avg_price, y = actual_pct)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(size = n, color = snapshot_label), alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(aes(color = snapshot_label, weight = n), method = "loess", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0,1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0,1)) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1,6), guide = "none") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    title    = "Polymarket Calibration Curve — Closed Binary Markets (2025)",
    subtitle = "Dashed line = perfect calibration · Each point = price bin at N hours before close",
    x = "Market Price (Implied Probability)", y = "Actual Resolution Rate", color = "Snapshot"
  )
```

## 2.2 Calibration Error by Snapshot Horizon

```{r calibration-error-summary}
cal_error <- snapshot_data %>%
  mutate(price_bin = round(snap_price * 20) / 20) %>%
  group_by(snapshot_label, price_bin) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), actual = mean(yes_resolution), predicted = mean(snap_price), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n >= 10) %>%
  group_by(snapshot_label) %>%
  summarise(
    weighted_cal_error = weighted.mean(abs(actual - predicted), w = n),
    n_bins             = n(),
    total_obs          = sum(n),
    .groups            = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(snapshot_label = factor(snapshot_label, levels = c("1mo","1w","3d","1d","6h","1h")))

ggplot(cal_error, aes(x = snapshot_label, y = weighted_cal_error)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = weighted_cal_error), width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(weighted_cal_error*100,1),"%")),
            vjust = -0.5, fontface = "bold", size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = COL_POS, high = COL_NEG) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    title    = "Average Calibration Error by Time Before Resolution",
    subtitle = "Lower = more accurate prices · Weighted by bin size",
    x = "Time Before Close", y = "Mean Absolute Calibration Error"
  )
```

## 2.3 Favorite–Longshot Bias

```{r favorite-longshot, fig.height=6}
fl_data <- snapshot_data %>%
  filter(snapshot_label == "1d") %>%
  mutate(
    price_bin    = cut(snap_price, breaks = seq(0,1,by=0.05),
                       include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE),

  ) %>%

  summarise(
    n = n(), actual = mean(yes_resolution), predicted = mean(snap_price),

ggplot(fl_data %>% filter(n >= 15), aes(x = bin_midpoint, y = bias)) +

    x = "Market Price Bin (1 day before close)", y = "Bias (Actual Resolution − Market Price)"
  )
```

## 2.4 Initial Price Calibration (Conditional)

**Important**: The naive aggregate "initial bias" (initial price minus resolution averaged across all markets) is misleading because it conflates the base rate of Yes resolutions (≈27%) with a default opening price near 50%. The correct test is *conditional*: for markets **opening in a given price bin**, does the resolution rate match that bin? This isolates real initial mispricing from compositional effects.

```{r initial-price-conditional, fig.height=6}
init_cal <- market_stats %>%
  filter(!is.na(initial_price), !is.na(yes_resolution), market_duration_h >= 24) %>%
  mutate(
    init_bin     = cut(initial_price, breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.05),
                       include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE),
    bin_midpoint = (init_bin - 1) * 0.05 + 0.025
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(init_bin)) %>%
  group_by(bin_midpoint) %>%
  summarise(
    n           = n(),
    actual_rate = mean(yes_resolution),
    avg_init    = mean(initial_price),
    cond_bias   = mean(yes_resolution) - mean(initial_price),
    .groups     = "drop"
  )

# Also compute for 1d snapshot for comparison
close_cal <- snapshot_data %>%
  filter(snapshot_label == "1d") %>%
  mutate(
    price_bin    = cut(snap_price, breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.05),
                       include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE),
    bin_midpoint = (price_bin - 1) * 0.05 + 0.025
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(price_bin)) %>%
  group_by(bin_midpoint) %>%
  summarise(
    n           = n(),
    actual_rate = mean(yes_resolution),
    avg_price   = mean(snap_price),
    cond_bias   = mean(yes_resolution) - mean(snap_price),
    .groups     = "drop"
  )

# Combine for overlay plot
init_vs_close_cal <- bind_rows(
  init_cal %>% mutate(stage = "At market open") %>% rename(price = avg_init),
  close_cal %>% mutate(stage = "1 day before close") %>% rename(price = avg_price)
)

ggplot(init_vs_close_cal %>% filter(n >= 15),
       aes(x = price, y = actual_rate, color = stage)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(aes(size = n), alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(aes(weight = n), method = "loess", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.5, 5), guide = "none") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("At market open" = COL_BLUE, "1 day before close" = COL_ORNG)) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    title    = "Conditional Calibration: Opening Price vs 1-Day-Before-Close",
    subtitle = "For each price bin: does the resolution rate match? Wider gap = more mispriced at open",
    x = "Price (Implied Probability)", y = "Actual Resolution Rate", color = NULL
  )
```

```{r initial-bias-conditional-bar, fig.height=5}
ggplot(init_cal %>% filter(n >= 15), aes(x = bin_midpoint, y = cond_bias)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_col(aes(fill = cond_bias), width = 0.04, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n, y = ifelse(cond_bias >= 0, cond_bias + 0.01, cond_bias - 0.01)),
            size = 2.8, color = "grey40") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = COL_NEG, mid = "grey80", high = COL_POS, midpoint = 0) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(
    title    = "Initial Price Bias (Conditional on Price Bin)",
    subtitle = "Within each opening-price bin: does resolution exceed the price? Numbers = market count",
    x = "Initial Price Bin", y = "Conditional Bias (Actual − Initial Price)"
  )
```

```{r initial-bias-conditional-summary}
cat("── Initial price calibration (conditional, within-bin) ──\n")
cat(sprintf("  Weighted mean absolute bias (initial):    %.2f%%\n",
    weighted.mean(abs(init_cal$cond_bias[init_cal$n >= 15]),
                  w = init_cal$n[init_cal$n >= 15]) * 100))
cat(sprintf("  Weighted mean absolute bias (1d close):   %.2f%%\n",
    weighted.mean(abs(close_cal$cond_bias[close_cal$n >= 15]),
                  w = close_cal$n[close_cal$n >= 15]) * 100))
cat("  (If initial >> close, new markets are genuinely mispriced and correct over time)\n")
```

```{r initial-bias-by-category, fig.height=5}
# Conditional initial bias by category (within-bin average, not raw aggregate)
init_cat_cond <- market_stats %>%
  filter(!is.na(initial_price), market_duration_h >= 24) %>%
  mutate(
    init_bin = cut(initial_price, breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.10),
                   include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE),
    bin_mid  = (init_bin - 1) * 0.10 + 0.05
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(init_bin)) %>%
  group_by(category, bin_mid) %>%
  summarise(
    n    = n(),
    bias = mean(yes_resolution) - mean(initial_price),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n >= 10) %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  summarise(
    n_bins        = n(),
    n_total       = sum(n),
    cond_init_bias = weighted.mean(bias, w = n),
    .groups       = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n_total >= 50)

ggplot(init_cat_cond, aes(x = reorder(category, cond_init_bias), y = cond_init_bias)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = cond_init_bias), width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(ifelse(cond_init_bias > 0, "+", ""),
                                round(cond_init_bias * 100, 1), "%"),
                y = cond_init_bias + sign(cond_init_bias) * 0.003),
            fontface = "bold", size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = COL_NEG, mid = "grey80", high = COL_POS, midpoint = 0) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title    = "Conditional Initial Price Bias by Category",
    subtitle = "Within-bin weighted average (corrects for base-rate composition)",
    x = NULL, y = "Conditional Bias (Actual − Initial Price)"
  )
```

# 3 · Category-Level Mispricings

## 3.1 Category Calibration Curves

```{r category-calibration, fig.height=10, fig.width=12}
cat_cal <- snapshot_data %>%
  filter(snapshot_label == "1d") %>%
  mutate(
    price_bin    = cut(snap_price, breaks = seq(0,1,by=0.10),
                       include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE),
    bin_midpoint = (price_bin - 1) * 0.10 + 0.05
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(price_bin)) %>%
  group_by(category, bin_midpoint) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), actual = mean(yes_resolution), predicted = mean(snap_price), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(cat_cal %>% filter(n >= 10), aes(x = predicted, y = actual)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(aes(size = n), color = COL_BLUE, alpha = 0.7) +

    subtitle = "Red line = actual calibration · Dashed = perfect · Bubble size = # markets",
    x = "Market Price (Implied Probability)", y = "Actual Resolution Rate"
  )
```

## 3.2 Category × Price Zone Bias Heatmap

```{r category-bias-heatmap, fig.height=7, fig.width=10}
# Helper to create price zone factor (used throughout)
make_price_zone <- function(price) {
  factor(
    case_when(
      price <= 0.15 ~ "Longshot (0-15%)",
      price <= 0.35 ~ "Unlikely (15-35%)",
      price <= 0.65 ~ "Toss-up (35-65%)",
      price <= 0.85 ~ "Likely (65-85%)",
      TRUE          ~ "Favorite (85-100%)"
    ),
    levels = c("Longshot (0-15%)", "Unlikely (15-35%)", "Toss-up (35-65%)",
               "Likely (65-85%)", "Favorite (85-100%)")
  )
}

cat_bias <- snapshot_data %>%
  filter(snapshot_label == "1d") %>%
  mutate(price_zone = make_price_zone(snap_price)) %>%
  group_by(category, price_zone) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), bias = mean(yes_resolution) - mean(snap_price), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n >= 10)

ggplot(cat_bias, aes(x = price_zone, y = category, fill = bias)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(ifelse(bias > 0,"+",""), round(bias*100,1),"%\n(n=",n,")")),
            size = 3.2, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = COL_NEG, mid = "white", high = COL_POS, midpoint = 0,
                       labels = percent, name = "Bias") +
  labs(
    title    = "Category × Price Zone Bias Heatmap — 1 Day Before Close",
    subtitle = "Green = underpriced (buy Yes) · Red = overpriced (buy No)",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

## 3.3 Aggregate Category Bias & Brier Score

```{r category-aggregate-stats}
cat_stats <- snapshot_data %>%
  filter(snapshot_label == "1d") %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  summarise(
    n_markets       = n(),
    avg_price       = mean(snap_price),
    resolution_rate = mean(yes_resolution),
    bias            = mean(yes_resolution) - mean(snap_price),
    brier_score     = mean((snap_price - yes_resolution)^2),
    abs_bias        = mean(abs(yes_resolution - snap_price)),
    .groups         = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(bias)))

cat_stats %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Category-Level Bias & Accuracy (1 day before close)")
```

# 4 · Volume & Liquidity Analysis

Thin markets are noisier. Let's check if bias patterns change when we weight by volume, and critically — which edges survive once we filter for markets a bot can actually trade.

## 4.1 Calibration by Volume Tier

```{r volume-weighted-calibration, fig.height=8}
vol_cal <- snapshot_data %>%
  filter(snapshot_label == "1d", !is.na(volume_num)) %>%
  mutate(
    vol_tier = factor(
      case_when(
        volume_num < 1000   ~ "Micro (<$1K)",
        volume_num < 10000  ~ "Small ($1K-$10K)",
        volume_num < 100000 ~ "Medium ($10K-$100K)",
        TRUE                ~ "Large (>$100K)"
      ),
      levels = c("Micro (<$1K)", "Small ($1K-$10K)", "Medium ($10K-$100K)", "Large (>$100K)")
    ),
    price_bin = round(snap_price * 10) / 10
  ) %>%
  group_by(vol_tier, price_bin) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), actual = mean(yes_resolution), predicted = mean(snap_price), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(vol_cal %>% filter(n >= 10), aes(x = predicted, y = actual)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(aes(size = n), color = COL_PURP, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(aes(weight = n), method = "loess", se = FALSE, color = COL_ORNG, linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ vol_tier, ncol = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0,1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0,1)) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1,5), guide = "none") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    title    = "Calibration by Market Volume Tier",
    subtitle = "Do thinner markets have worse calibration?",
    x = "Market Price", y = "Actual Resolution Rate"
  )
```

```{r volume-brier}
vol_brier <- snapshot_data %>%
  filter(snapshot_label == "1d", !is.na(volume_num)) %>%

        volume_num < 1000   ~ "Micro (<$1K)",
        volume_num < 10000  ~ "Small ($1K-$10K)",

      ),
```

## 4.2 Liquidity-Filtered Edge Survival

**Critical for bot**: Edges in markets with < $10K volume are un-tradeable (slippage would eat the edge). Here we recompute the exploitable segment table restricted to liquid markets.

```{r liquidity-filtered-edges, fig.height=7, fig.width=10}
liquid_bias <- snapshot_data %>%
  filter(snapshot_label == "1d", !is.na(volume_num)) %>%
  mutate(
    liquid      = volume_num >= MIN_VOLUME,
    price_zone  = make_price_zone(snap_price)

# Compare bias all vs liquid-only
liquid_compare <- liquid_bias %>%
  group_by(price_zone, liquid) %>%
  summarise(
    n    = n(),
    bias = mean(yes_resolution) - mean(snap_price),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n >= 10) %>%
  mutate(liquid_label = ifelse(liquid, paste0("Liquid (≥$", MIN_VOLUME/1000, "K)"), "All Markets"))

# Category × zone for liquid only
liquid_cat_bias <- liquid_bias %>%
  filter(liquid) %>%
  mutate(price_zone = make_price_zone(snap_price)) %>%
  group_by(category, price_zone) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), bias = mean(yes_resolution) - mean(snap_price), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n >= 10)

ggplot(liquid_cat_bias, aes(x = price_zone, y = category, fill = bias)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(ifelse(bias > 0,"+",""), round(bias*100,1),"%\n(n=",n,")")),
            size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = COL_NEG, mid = "white", high = COL_POS, midpoint = 0,
                       labels = percent, name = "Bias") +
  labs(

  ) +

```

```{r liquidity-edge-survival}

all_seg <- snapshot_data %>%

  filter(snapshot_label == "1d", !is.na(volume_num), volume_num >= MIN_VOLUME) %>%
  mutate(price_zone = make_price_zone(snap_price)) %>%
  group_by(category, price_zone) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), bias = mean(yes_resolution) - mean(snap_price), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n >= MIN_N_EXPLOIT, abs(bias) > 0.03)

cat(sprintf("── Liquidity filter impact ──\n"))

cat(sprintf("  Exploitable segments (volume ≥ $%dK):   %d\n", MIN_VOLUME/1000, nrow(liq_seg)))
cat(sprintf("  Survival rate:                           %.0f%%\n",
            nrow(liq_seg) / max(nrow(all_seg), 1) * 100))
```

# 5 · Market Duration Effects

```{r duration-bias}
duration_bias <- market_stats %>%
  filter(!is.na(market_duration_h), !is.na(initial_price), market_duration_h >= 1) %>%
  inner_join(
    snapshot_data %>%
      filter(snapshot_label == "1d") %>%
      select(id, snap_price) %>%
      rename(price_1d = snap_price),
    by = "id"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    duration_tier = factor(
      case_when(
        market_duration_h < 24   ~ "< 1 day",
        market_duration_h < 168  ~ "1-7 days",
        market_duration_h < 720  ~ "1-4 weeks",
        market_duration_h < 2160 ~ "1-3 months",
        TRUE                     ~ "> 3 months"
      ),
      levels = c("< 1 day","1-7 days","1-4 weeks","1-3 months","> 3 months")
    )
  ) %>%
  # Conditional bias within price bins (avoids base-rate contamination)
  mutate(init_bin = round(initial_price * 10) / 10) %>%
  group_by(duration_tier) %>%
  summarise(
    n             = n(),
    init_bias     = mean(yes_resolution - initial_price),
    final_bias    = mean(yes_resolution - price_1d),
    price_range   = mean(price_range, na.rm = TRUE),
    resolution_r  = mean(yes_resolution),
    brier_initial = mean((initial_price - yes_resolution)^2),
    .groups       = "drop"
  )

duration_bias %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Bias & Calibration by Market Duration")
```

```{r duration-bias-plot, fig.height=5}
    init_bias  = "At market open",

ggplot(duration_long, aes(x = duration_tier, y = bias, fill = stage)) +
```

# 6 · Late-Stage Price Signals

When the price moves substantially in the final week, is that move informative about the resolution? If yes, **following the move** (momentum) is a tradeable signal. If no (or reverse), **fading the move** is.

```{r late-stage-moves, fig.height=5}
snap_divergence <- snapshot_data %>%
  select(id, snapshot_label, snap_price, yes_resolution, category, volume_num) %>%
  filter(snapshot_label %in% c("1w", "1d")) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = snapshot_label, values_from = snap_price,
              names_prefix = "price_") %>%
  filter(!is.na(price_1w), !is.na(price_1d)) %>%
  mutate(
    late_move     = price_1d - price_1w,
    move_correct  = (late_move > 0 & yes_resolution == 1) | (late_move < 0 & yes_resolution == 0),
    move_size_abs = abs(late_move),
    move_bucket   = factor(
      case_when(
        move_size_abs < 0.05 ~ "Tiny (<5pp)",
        move_size_abs < 0.15 ~ "Small (5-15pp)",
        move_size_abs < 0.30 ~ "Medium (15-30pp)",
        TRUE                 ~ "Large (>30pp)"
      ),
      levels = c("Tiny (<5pp)", "Small (5-15pp)", "Medium (15-30pp)", "Large (>30pp)")
    )
  )

late_move_summary <- snap_divergence %>%
  filter(move_size_abs >= 0.05) %>%
  group_by(move_bucket) %>%
  summarise(
    n               = n(),
    pct_correct     = mean(move_correct),
    avg_move        = mean(late_move),
    resolution_rate = mean(yes_resolution),
    .groups         = "drop"
  )

ggplot(late_move_summary, aes(x = move_bucket, y = pct_correct)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = pct_correct > 0.5), width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(pct_correct*100,1),"%\nn=",n)),
            vjust = -0.4, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = COL_NEG, "TRUE" = COL_POS)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(
    title    = "Late-Stage Price Moves (1 week → 1 day): Are They Informative?",
    subtitle = "Above 50% = follow the move (momentum) · Below 50% = fade the move",
    x = "Size of Move (1w → 1d)", y = "% Where Move Was in Correct Direction"
  )
```

```{r late-stage-by-category, fig.height=6}
# Statistical test: is the momentum signal significant per category?
late_cat <- snap_divergence %>%
  filter(move_size_abs >= 0.05) %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  summarise(
    n           = n(),
    pct_correct = mean(move_correct),
    p_value     = if (n() >= 20) binom.test(sum(move_correct), n(), 0.5)$p.value else NA_real_,
    .groups     = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n >= 20) %>%
  mutate(significant = !is.na(p_value) & p_value < 0.05)

ggplot(late_cat, aes(x = reorder(category, pct_correct), y = pct_correct)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = significant), width = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(pct_correct*100,1),"% (n=",n,
                                ifelse(significant, " *", ""), ")")),
            hjust = -0.1, size = 3.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = COL_NEUT, "TRUE" = COL_POS),
                    labels = c("FALSE" = "Not significant", "TRUE" = "p < 0.05")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, 0.9)) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title    = "Late-Stage Momentum Signal by Category (1w → 1d)",
    subtitle = "* = statistically significant (binomial test, p < 0.05)",
    x = NULL, y = "% of Moves in Correct Direction", fill = NULL
  )
```

# 7 · Temporal Stability of Edges

**Critical for bot**: A bias that appeared once is noise; a bias that persists monthly is structural. Here we track the top exploitable segments over time to see which edges a bot can rely on.

```{r temporal-setup}
# Add close month to snapshot data
snap_with_time <- snapshot_data %>%
  filter(snapshot_label == "1d") %>%
  left_join(
    market_stats %>% select(id, closed_dt),
    by = "id"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(closed_dt)) %>%
  mutate(
    close_month   = floor_date(closed_dt, "month"),
    close_quarter = paste0(year(closed_dt), "-Q", quarter(closed_dt)),
    price_zone    = make_price_zone(snap_price)
  )
```

## 7.1 Rolling Monthly Bias for Top Segments

```{r rolling-monthly-bias, fig.height=8, fig.width=12}
# Identify the top exploitable segments (from all-data analysis)
top_segments <- snapshot_data %>%
  filter(snapshot_label == "1d") %>%
  mutate(price_zone = make_price_zone(snap_price)) %>%
  group_by(category, price_zone) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), bias = mean(yes_resolution) - mean(snap_price), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n >= 30, abs(bias) > 0.04) %>%
  slice_max(abs(bias), n = 8) %>%
  mutate(segment = paste(category, "×", price_zone))

# Monthly bias for these segments
monthly_bias <- snap_with_time %>%
  mutate(segment = paste(category, "×", price_zone)) %>%
  filter(segment %in% top_segments$segment) %>%
  group_by(segment, close_month) %>%
  summarise(
    n    = n(),
    bias = mean(yes_resolution) - mean(snap_price),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n >= 5)   # need at least 5 markets per month to be meaningful

if (nrow(monthly_bias) > 0) {
  ggplot(monthly_bias, aes(x = close_month, y = bias)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
    geom_line(color = COL_BLUE, linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_point(aes(size = n), color = COL_BLUE, alpha = 0.7) +
    facet_wrap(~ segment, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_x_datetime(date_labels = "%b %Y", date_breaks = "1 month") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.5, 4), name = "n markets") +
    labs(
      title    = "Rolling Monthly Bias — Top Exploitable Segments",
      subtitle = "Persistent ≠ one-off. A reliable edge should be visible across most months.",
      x = NULL, y = "Monthly Bias (Actual − Price)"
    ) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
} else {
  cat("Not enough data for monthly segment breakdown.\n")
}
```

## 7.2 Edge Persistence Score

```{r edge-persistence}
# For each top segment: in how many months was the bias in the "expected" direction?
persistence <- snap_with_time %>%
  mutate(segment = paste(category, "×", price_zone)) %>%
  filter(segment %in% top_segments$segment) %>%
  group_by(segment, close_month) %>%
  summarise(
    n            = n(),
    monthly_bias = mean(yes_resolution) - mean(snap_price),
    .groups      = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n >= 5) %>%
  left_join(top_segments %>% select(segment, bias), by = "segment") %>%
  rename(overall_bias = bias) %>%
  mutate(same_direction = sign(monthly_bias) == sign(overall_bias)) %>%
  group_by(segment, overall_bias) %>%
  summarise(
    n_months        = n(),
    months_correct  = sum(same_direction),
    persistence_pct = mean(same_direction) * 100,
    avg_monthly_n   = mean(n),
    .groups         = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(persistence_pct))

persistence %>%
  mutate(
    overall_bias    = paste0(round(overall_bias * 100, 1), "%"),
    persistence_pct = paste0(round(persistence_pct, 0), "%"),
    avg_monthly_n   = round(avg_monthly_n, 0)
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Edge Persistence: How Many Months Does the Bias Appear?")
```

# 8 · Exploitable Pattern Summary

## 8.1 Gross Edge Table

```{r gross-edge-table}
exploitable <- snapshot_data %>%
  filter(snapshot_label == "1d") %>%
  mutate(price_zone = make_price_zone(snap_price)) %>%
  group_by(category, price_zone) %>%
  summarise(
    n_markets   = n(),
    avg_price   = mean(snap_price),
    actual_rate = mean(yes_resolution),
    bias        = mean(yes_resolution) - mean(snap_price),
    edge_pct    = bias / avg_price * 100,
    brier       = mean((snap_price - yes_resolution)^2),
    .groups     = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n_markets >= MIN_N_EXPLOIT, abs(bias) > 0.03) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(bias)))

exploitable %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric) & !n_markets, ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  head(20) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Top 20 Most Exploitable Category × Price Zone Combinations (|bias| > 3%, n ≥ 15)")
```

## 8.2 Transaction Cost–Adjusted Edge Table

**The critical filter**: gross edges are meaningless without accounting for the ~2% spread and ~2% winner fee. A segment is only tradeable if the net edge after costs exceeds ~1%.

```{r cost-adjusted-edges}
exploitable_net <- exploitable %>%
  mutate(
    strategy   = ifelse(bias > 0, "Buy Yes", "Buy No"),
    # Win probability and price depend on which side we're trading
    win_prob   = ifelse(bias > 0, actual_rate, 1 - actual_rate),
    entry_price = ifelse(bias > 0, avg_price, 1 - avg_price),
    # Costs
    spread     = SPREAD_COST,
    fee_cost   = WINNER_FEE * win_prob,   # fee only applies to wins
    total_cost = spread + fee_cost,
    # Net edge after costs
    gross_edge = abs(bias),
    net_edge   = gross_edge - total_cost,
    # Expected P&L per $1 bet (accounting for costs)
    gross_pl   = ifelse(
      bias > 0,
      actual_rate * (1 / avg_price - 1) - (1 - actual_rate),
      (1 - actual_rate) * (1 / (1 - avg_price) - 1) - actual_rate
    ),
    net_pl     = gross_pl - total_cost,
    tradeable  = net_edge > MIN_EDGE_NET
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(net_edge))

exploitable_net %>%
  select(category, price_zone, n_markets, strategy, gross_edge, spread,
         fee_cost, total_cost, net_edge, net_pl, tradeable) %>%
  mutate(
    across(c(gross_edge, spread, fee_cost, total_cost, net_edge, net_pl),
           ~ paste0(round(.x * 100, 1), "%")),
    tradeable = ifelse(tradeable, "✅ YES", "❌ NO")
  ) %>%
  head(20) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    caption = sprintf("Cost-Adjusted Edges (spread=%.0f%%, winner fee=%.0f%%, min net edge=%.0f%%)",
                      SPREAD_COST*100, WINNER_FEE*100, MIN_EDGE_NET*100)
  )
```

```{r cost-adjusted-plot, fig.height=6}
plot_data <- exploitable_net %>%
  head(15) %>%
  mutate(label = paste(category, price_zone, sep = "\n"))

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = reorder(label, net_pl), y = net_pl)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = tradeable), width = 0.6) +

            hjust = ifelse(plot_data$net_pl >= 0, -0.1, 1.1),
            size = 3.3, fontface = "bold") +

                    labels = c("TRUE" = "Net profitable", "FALSE" = "Costs > edge")) +

    x = NULL, y = "Net Expected Profit per $1 Wagered", fill = NULL
  )
```

## 8.3 Bootstrap Confidence Intervals

```{r bootstrap-ci, cache=TRUE}
snap_1d <- snapshot_data %>%
  filter(snapshot_label == "1d") %>%
  mutate(price_zone = make_price_zone(snap_price))

boot_bias_fn <- function(data, indices) {
  d <- data[indices, ]
  mean(d$yes_resolution) - mean(d$snap_price)
}

# Bootstrap the tradeable (or top) segments
top_for_ci <- exploitable_net %>% head(15) %>% select(category, price_zone)

ci_results <- pmap_dfr(top_for_ci, function(category, price_zone) {
  seg <- snap_1d %>% filter(category == .env$category, price_zone == .env$price_zone)
  n_obs      <- nrow(seg)
  point_bias <- mean(seg$yes_resolution) - mean(seg$snap_price)

  ci_lo <- NA_real_
  ci_hi <- NA_real_

  if (n_obs >= 30) {
    bo <- boot(seg, boot_bias_fn, R = 2000)
    ci <- boot.ci(bo, type = "perc")
    if (!is.null(ci$percent)) {
      ci_lo <- ci$percent[4]
      ci_hi <- ci$percent[5]
    }
  }

  tibble(
    category    = category,
    price_zone  = price_zone,
    n_obs       = n_obs,
    point_bias  = point_bias,
    ci_lo       = ci_lo,
    ci_hi       = ci_hi,
    significant = !is.na(ci_lo) & (ci_lo > 0 | ci_hi < 0)
  )
})

ci_results %>%
  mutate(
    across(c(point_bias, ci_lo, ci_hi), ~ paste0(round(.x * 100, 2), "%")),
    significant = ifelse(significant, "✅ YES", "no")
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Bootstrap 95% CIs — Which Edges Are Statistically Real?")
```

```{r ci-plot, fig.height=6}
ci_plot <- ci_results %>%
  filter(!is.na(ci_lo)) %>%
  mutate(label = paste(category, price_zone, sep = "\n"))

ggplot(ci_plot, aes(x = reorder(label, point_bias), y = point_bias)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lo, ymax = ci_hi, color = significant),
                width = 0.3, linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(aes(color = significant), size = 3.5) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("TRUE" = COL_POS, "FALSE" = COL_NEG),
    labels = c("TRUE" = "CI excludes zero (reliable)", "FALSE" = "CI crosses zero (noise)")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title    = "Exploitable Edges with Bootstrap 95% Confidence Intervals",
    subtitle = "Green = statistically significant · Red = likely noise",
    x = NULL, y = "Bias (Actual − Market Price)", color = NULL
  )
```

## 8.4 Kelly Criterion Position Sizing

For each tradeable edge, optimal bet sizing via the Kelly criterion. Half-Kelly is recommended in practice (accounts for edge estimation error).

```{r kelly-sizing}
kelly_table <- exploitable_net %>%
  filter(tradeable) %>%
  mutate(
    # For a binary bet: Kelly f* = (p*b - q) / b
    # where p = win prob, q = 1-p, b = net payout odds
    # On Polymarket: if entry price = c, payout = 1, so b = (1-cost)/c - 1 roughly
    # Simplified: edge / variance approach
    # f* = net_edge / (entry_price * (1 - entry_price))  (approx for binary)
    b           = (1 - total_cost) / entry_price - 1,   # net payout ratio
    q           = 1 - win_prob,
    kelly_full  = pmax(0, (win_prob * b - q) / b),
    kelly_half  = kelly_full / 2,
    # Expected log growth at half-Kelly
    growth_rate = win_prob * log(1 + kelly_half * b) + q * log(1 - kelly_half)
  ) %>%
  select(category, price_zone, strategy, n_markets, net_edge, win_prob,
         kelly_full, kelly_half, growth_rate) %>%
  arrange(desc(growth_rate))

kelly_table %>%
  mutate(
    net_edge    = paste0(round(net_edge * 100, 1), "%"),
    win_prob    = paste0(round(win_prob * 100, 1), "%"),
    kelly_full  = paste0(round(kelly_full * 100, 1), "%"),
    kelly_half  = paste0(round(kelly_half * 100, 1), "%"),
    growth_rate = paste0(round(growth_rate * 100, 3), "%")
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Kelly Criterion Sizing — Tradeable Segments Only (after costs)")
```

## 8.5 Composite Exploitability Score

A single score the bot can compute in real-time for any market. Combines calibration bias, liquidity, statistical significance, and temporal persistence.

```{r composite-score}
# Build a scoring table for each tradeable segment
composite <- exploitable_net %>%
  filter(tradeable) %>%
  mutate(segment = paste(category, "×", price_zone)) %>%
  left_join(
    ci_results %>% select(category, price_zone, significant, ci_lo, ci_hi),
    by = c("category", "price_zone")
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    persistence %>% select(segment, persistence_pct, n_months),
    by = "segment"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Component scores (0-1)
    edge_score       = pmin(abs(net_edge) / 0.10, 1),               # net edge scaled to 10%
    stat_score       = ifelse(significant, 1, 0),                    # binary: CI excludes 0?
    persist_score    = coalesce(persistence_pct / 100, 0.5),         # % of months bias persists
    sample_score     = pmin(n_markets / 500, 1),                     # scaled sample size
    # Weighted composite
    composite_score  = 0.35 * edge_score +
                       0.25 * stat_score +
                       0.25 * persist_score +
                       0.15 * sample_score
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(composite_score))

composite %>%
  select(segment, strategy, net_edge, edge_score, stat_score, persist_score,
         sample_score, composite_score) %>%
  mutate(
    net_edge = paste0(round(net_edge * 100, 1), "%"),
    across(c(edge_score, stat_score, persist_score, sample_score, composite_score),
           ~ round(.x, 2))
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    caption = "Composite Exploitability Score (0-1) — Higher = more reliably tradeable"
  )
```

# 9 · Simulated Backtest

**The ultimate test**: if we had traded every qualifying market in the exploitable segments, what would the P&L look like?

```{r backtest-setup}
# Identify all markets in tradeable segments, using 1d snapshot as entry
tradeable_segments <- exploitable_net %>%
  filter(tradeable) %>%
  select(category, price_zone, strategy)

backtest_markets <- snapshot_data %>%
  filter(snapshot_label == "1d") %>%
  mutate(price_zone = make_price_zone(snap_price)) %>%
  inner_join(tradeable_segments, by = c("category", "price_zone")) %>%
  left_join(market_stats %>% select(id, closed_dt), by = "id") %>%
  filter(!is.na(closed_dt)) %>%
  arrange(closed_dt) %>%
  mutate(
    # Entry price and resolution
    entry_price = ifelse(strategy == "Buy Yes", snap_price, 1 - snap_price),
    won         = ifelse(strategy == "Buy Yes", yes_resolution == 1, yes_resolution == 0),
    # P&L per $1 bet
    gross_pnl   = ifelse(won, (1 - entry_price), -entry_price),
    # Costs: spread on entry, fee on win
    cost        = SPREAD_COST + ifelse(won, WINNER_FEE, 0),
    net_pnl     = gross_pnl - cost,
    # Cumulative
    cum_gross   = cumsum(gross_pnl),
    cum_net     = cumsum(net_pnl),
    bet_num     = row_number()
  )

cat(sprintf("── Backtest universe ──\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Tradeable segments:  %d\n", nrow(tradeable_segments)))
cat(sprintf("  Total qualifying bets: %d\n", nrow(backtest_markets)))
cat(sprintf("  Win rate:              %.1f%%\n", mean(backtest_markets$won) * 100))
cat(sprintf("  Gross P&L (total):     $%.2f per $1/bet\n", sum(backtest_markets$gross_pnl)))
cat(sprintf("  Net P&L (total):       $%.2f per $1/bet\n", sum(backtest_markets$net_pnl)))
cat(sprintf("  Net P&L per bet:       %.2f¢\n", mean(backtest_markets$net_pnl) * 100))
```

```{r backtest-cumpl, fig.height=5}
  geom_line(aes(y = cum_gross, color = "Gross (no costs)"), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_line(aes(y = cum_net, color = "Net (after costs)"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Gross (no costs)" = COL_NEUT, "Net (after costs)" = COL_POS)) +

                       nrow(backtest_markets), SPREAD_COST*100, WINNER_FEE*100),

  )
```

## 9.2 Drawdown & Risk Metrics

```{r backtest-risk, fig.height=5}
# Compute drawdown
backtest_markets <- backtest_markets %>%
  mutate(
    peak_net  = cummax(cum_net),
    drawdown  = cum_net - peak_net
  )

max_dd     <- min(backtest_markets$drawdown)
total_bets <- nrow(backtest_markets)
total_net  <- sum(backtest_markets$net_pnl)
avg_net    <- mean(backtest_markets$net_pnl)
sd_net     <- sd(backtest_markets$net_pnl)
sharpe_per_bet <- avg_net / sd_net  # per-bet Sharpe analog

ggplot(backtest_markets, aes(x = bet_num, y = drawdown)) +
  geom_area(fill = COL_NEG, alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(color = COL_NEG, linewidth = 0.6) +
  labs(
    title    = "Drawdown (Net P&L)",
    subtitle = sprintf("Max drawdown: $%.2f | Sharpe (per bet): %.3f", max_dd, sharpe_per_bet),
    x = "Bet Number", y = "Drawdown ($)"
  )
```

```{r backtest-summary-table}
# Monthly returns
monthly_bt <- backtest_markets %>%
  mutate(month = floor_date(closed_dt, "month")) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(
    n_bets     = n(),
    net_pnl    = sum(net_pnl),
    win_rate   = mean(won),
    .groups    = "drop"
  )

tibble(
  Metric = c("Total bets", "Win rate", "Gross P&L", "Net P&L",
             "Net P&L per bet", "Std dev per bet", "Sharpe (per bet)",
             "Max drawdown", "Profitable months"),
  Value = c(
    total_bets,
    paste0(round(mean(backtest_markets$won)*100, 1), "%"),
    paste0("$", round(sum(backtest_markets$gross_pnl), 2)),
    paste0("$", round(total_net, 2)),
    paste0(round(avg_net*100, 2), "¢"),
    paste0(round(sd_net*100, 2), "¢"),
    round(sharpe_per_bet, 3),
    paste0("$", round(max_dd, 2)),
    paste0(sum(monthly_bt$net_pnl > 0), "/", nrow(monthly_bt))
  )
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Backtest Summary — Flat $1 Bets on All Tradeable Segments")
```

```{r monthly-returns, fig.height=4}
}
```

# 10 · Bot Implementation Notes

```{r bot-notes, results='asis'}
# Gather key results for the summary
n_sig_ci      <- sum(ci_results$significant, na.rm = TRUE)
n_tradeable_f <- sum(exploitable_net$tradeable, na.rm = TRUE)

overall_bias <- snapshot_data %>%
  filter(snapshot_label == "1d") %>%
  summarise(bias = mean(yes_resolution) - mean(snap_price)) %>%
  pull(bias)

best_segment <- exploitable_net %>% filter(tradeable) %>% slice(1)

cat("## Entry Signals\n\n")
cat("The bot should evaluate each new binary market against these criteria:\n\n")
cat("1. **Category**: Match market tags to category rules\n")
cat("2. **Price zone**: Current Yes price maps to one of 5 zones\n")
cat(sprintf("3. **Volume threshold**: Only trade markets with ≥ $%dK volume\n", MIN_VOLUME/1000))
cat(sprintf("4. **Net edge threshold**: Only enter if estimated net edge > %.0f%%\n", MIN_EDGE_NET*100))
cat("5. **Composite score**: Prefer segments with composite score > 0.5\n\n")

cat("## Position Sizing\n\n")
cat("- Use **half-Kelly** fractions from §8.4\n")
cat("- Cap any single position at 5% of bankroll\n")
cat("- Cap total exposure at 30% of bankroll (diversification)\n\n")

cat("## Risk Limits\n\n")
cat("- **Daily loss limit**: Pause trading after 5% bankroll drawdown in a day\n")
cat("- **Monthly review**: Recompute all bias tables monthly with fresh data\n")
cat("- **Edge decay**: If a segment's rolling 30-day bias flips sign, stop trading it\n")
cat("- **Minimum sample**: Don't trade a segment with < 30 historical resolved markets\n\n")

cat("## Key Findings\n\n")

cat(sprintf("- **Overall market bias** (1d before close): %+.1f%%. %s.\n",
  overall_bias * 100,
  ifelse(abs(overall_bias) > 0.01,
    ifelse(overall_bias > 0, "Markets slightly underprice Yes", "Markets slightly overprice Yes"),
    "Markets are approximately well-calibrated overall")))

cat(sprintf("- **Tradeable edges after costs**: %d segments survive (out of %d gross)\n",
  n_tradeable_f, nrow(exploitable)))

cat(sprintf("- **Statistically significant edges**: %d/%d top segments have bootstrap CIs excluding zero\n",
  n_sig_ci, nrow(ci_results)))

if (nrow(best_segment) > 0) {
  cat(sprintf("- **Best net edge**: %s × %s (%s, net edge %+.1f%%, n=%d)\n",
    best_segment$category, best_segment$price_zone, best_segment$strategy,
    best_segment$net_edge * 100, best_segment$n_markets))
}

cat(sprintf("- **Backtest result**: $%.2f net P&L on %d $1 bets (%.2f¢ per bet avg)\n",
  total_net, total_bets, avg_net * 100))

cat(sprintf("- **Max drawdown**: $%.2f · Sharpe per bet: %.3f\n", max_dd, sharpe_per_bet))

# Persistence insight
if (nrow(persistence) > 0) {
  best_persist <- persistence %>% slice(1)
  cat(sprintf("- **Most persistent edge**: %s — bias in correct direction %s of months\n",
    best_persist$segment, paste0(round(best_persist$persistence_pct, 0), "%")))
}

cat("\n\n---\n\n")
cat("> **Disclaimer**: Past calibration patterns do not guarantee future exploitability.")
cat(" Transaction costs, slippage, and market evolution may erode these edges.")
cat(" Always paper-trade or use minimal size before scaling.")
cat(" The cost assumptions above (", SPREAD_COST*100, "% spread, ", WINNER_FEE*100,
    "% winner fee) are estimates — actual costs depend on market conditions and order size.\n")
```
